reference: Installed file(1) from the isolated reference PATH, compared byte-for-byte with the candidate; deterministic signatures are written by Bash printf. The metadata contract checks Bash type/help builtins against the loadable's documented short description. Custom classifier descriptions and implementation identity are independent contracts, not libmagic parity.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and help metadata
Empty, ASCII text, and opaque-data fallback classes
stdin classification, brief output, path labels, --, and directories
Missing-path status and diagnostic stream behavior
Explicit -E, brief combinations, continuation, no-operand usage and ordinary ENOTDIR errors
Guest pass 3 G51: -L/-h, -i/--mime, --mime-type, --mime-encoding, symlink targets, libmagic text encodings and line-terminator notes, PNG/GIF/gzip/bzip2/xz headers, scripts, HTML and XML.
exclusions: The classifier's full curated signature catalog is not exhaustively enumerated; the suite samples broad fallback, document, and binary paths.
No fixture uses a host path, real device, network, credentials, or privileged operation; no operation case needs deferral.
The installed reference rejects --error; only -E is supported as the filesystem error option. Full libmagic and detailed ELF output remain outside the custom classifier contract.

cases.purpose: Check through Bash builtins that file is registered as a builtin and that help exposes its documented short description.
cases.script:
type -t file
h=$(help -d file)
case $h in *"Identify file types via magic-byte signatures."*) printf 'help-ok\n' ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac

cases.purpose: Compare brief classification of empty, ordinary ASCII, and short opaque-byte files, covering the basic fallback categories.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf 'plain words\n' > text
printf '\001\002\003' > opaque
file -b empty text opaque

cases.purpose: Check object and array JSON-looking prefixes after optional leading whitespace.
cases.script:
printf '{"key":1}\n' > object
printf '  [1,2]\n' > array
file -b object array

cases.purpose: Compare stable PEM certificate, certificate-request, and PGP message armor labels using public marker lines.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' > cert
printf '%s\n' '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----' > request-marker
printf '%s\n' '-----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----' > pgp-marker
file -b cert request-marker pgp-marker

cases.purpose: Check recognition of the conventional 0x55aa DOS/MBR signature at byte offsets 510-511 in a 512-byte relative fixture.
cases.script:
printf '\0%.0s' {1..510} > mbr
printf '\125\252' >> mbr
file -b mbr

cases.purpose: Check that a single stdin operand reads the stream and that brief mode suppresses the input label.
cases.script: printf 'stdin text\n' | file -b -

cases.purpose: Check aligned labels for a spaced path, option-looking path after --, empty file and directory.
cases.script:
printf 'sample\n' > 'two words'
printf 'dash name\n' > ./-leading
: > empty
mkdir folder
file -- 'two words' ./-leading empty folder

cases.purpose: Continue after a missing operand with a stdout diagnostic and success status by default.
cases.script:
printf 'present\n' > present
file missing present

cases.purpose: A missing operand uses the reference default diagnostic and success status.
cases.script: file missing

cases.purpose: Brief output suppresses labels for both missing and readable operands.
cases.script:
printf 'present\n' > longer
file -b missing longer

cases.purpose: The explicit -E error option reports an error status for a missing operand.
cases.script: file -E missing

cases.purpose: With -E, inspect continuation and diagnostic streams when a missing operand precedes a valid operand.
cases.script:
printf 'present\n' > present
file -E missing present

cases.purpose: Alignment uses the literal stdin operand length even though its displayed label is /dev/stdin.
cases.script:
printf 'text\n' > a
printf 'stdin text\n' | file a -

cases.purpose: Label width is recalculated on every builtin invocation.
cases.script:
: > longest_name
: > a
file a longest_name
file a

cases.purpose: A missing intermediate path component follows the same default policy.
cases.script: file absent/child

cases.purpose: The classifier gives file 5.46's shebang and HTML descriptions with the text encoding (checked against GNU in regressions/file.json) and keeps its concise Netpbm description, which is not full libmagic output.
cases.script:
printf '#!/bin/sh
printf hello
' > sample.sh
printf '<!doctype html><html><body>hello</body></html>
' > page.html
printf 'P2
1 1
255
0
' > image.pgm
file -b sample.sh page.html image.pgm
cases.stdout:
POSIX shell script, ASCII text executable
HTML document, ASCII text
Netpbm image data

cases.purpose: Preserve the existing implementation identity banner as a custom metadata contract; do not compare it to the reference version banner or count it as operation coverage.
cases.script:
file --version
file -v

cases.purpose: Long brief mode combines with -E without restoring a path label; processing continues after the missing input.
cases.script:
printf 'present\n' > very_long_present
file --brief -E missing very_long_present

cases.purpose: The explicitly supported -bE short-option bundle gives the same missing-input status and brief diagnostic as separate options.
cases.script: file -bE missing

cases.purpose: An invocation without operands returns the installed reference usage status and a diagnostic.
cases.script: file

cases.purpose: Ordinary ENOTDIR operands follow the same default stdout diagnostic and success status as absent paths.
cases.script:
printf 'ordinary file\n' > parent
file parent/child

cases.purpose: The installed file reference has no --error alias for -E; reject it with usage status and a diagnostic.
cases.script: file --error missing

cases.purpose: G51: a symbolic link is described with its target, a dangling one as broken; -h keeps that default.
cases.script:
touch t
ln -s t l
ln -s nowhere broken
file l broken
file -h l

cases.purpose: G51: -L and --dereference describe what a link points to; a dangling link then cannot be opened.
cases.script:
touch t
ln -s t l
ln -s nowhere broken
mkdir d
ln -s d ld
file -L l broken ld
file --dereference l
file -bL l

cases.purpose: G51: -i/--mime prints type and charset, --mime-type and --mime-encoding one of them, for text, empty, directory, link, PNG and data inputs.
cases.script:
echo hi > f
printf 'h\303\251\n' > u
printf 'h\351\n' > l1
: > e
mkdir d
ln -s f lk
printf '\211PNG\r\n\032\n\0\0\0\rIHDR\0\0\0\1\0\0\0\1\010\002\0\0\0' > img
printf '\1\2\3' > bin
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho\n' > s
file -i f u l1 e d lk img bin s
file --mime f
file --mime-type f img s d
file --mime-encoding f u l1 img
file -bi f

cases.purpose: G51: text notes CRLF, CR, mixed CRLF/LF and missing line terminators, very long lines, escape sequences and overstriking.
cases.script:
printf 'a\r\n' > crlf
printf 'a\rb\r' > cr
printf 'a\r\nb\n' > mixed
printf 'abc' > nonl
printf '%0301d\n' 0 > long
printf '\033[1m\n' > esc
printf 'x\010y\n' > bs
file crlf cr mixed nonl long esc bs

cases.purpose: G51: ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, ISO-8859 and non-ISO extended-ASCII text are named as file 5.46 names them.
cases.script:
printf 'hi\n' > a
printf 'h\303\251\n' > u
printf '\357\273\277hi\r\n' > bom
printf 'h\351\n' > latin
printf '\200\201x\n' > ext
file -b a u bom latin ext

cases.purpose: G51: PNG and GIF descriptions carry the header's size, depth, colour type and interlace, or version.
G51: #! scripts, HTML and XML get file 5.46's names with the text encoding and notes.
cases.script: printf '#!/bin/sh echo ' > s printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash ' > b printf '#!/usr/bin/env python3 ' > p printf '#!/usr/bin/perl -w ' > pl printf '#!/usr/bin/foo ' > g printf '#!/usr/bin/env sh ' > es printf ' ' > h printf ' \303\251 ' > x file -b s b p pl g es h x

cases.purpose: G51: gzip (name, time, flags, OS, size), bzip2 block size and xz checksum details.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC
printf '\037\213\010\010\001\0\0\0\002\003ab\0xyz\006\0\0\0' > a.gz
printf '\037\213\010\0\0\0\0\0\004\0xxxx\001\0\0\0' > b.gz
printf 'BZh9' > c.bz2
printf '\3757zXZ\0\0\004' > d.xz
file -b a.gz b.gz c.bz2 d.xz

cases.purpose: G51: FIFO naming and MIME types for directory, FIFO and empty files.
cases.script:
mkfifo p
mkdir d
: > e
file p d e
file -i p d e

cases.purpose: G71: -f NAMEFILE / -fNAMEFILE / --files-from[=]NAMEFILE describe each listed name, aligned among themselves, when the option is reached and with the options before it; '-' reads names from stdin; options may follow operands.
cases.script:
printf 'x\n' > a
printf '#!/bin/sh\n' > longname.sh
printf 'a\nlongname.sh\n' > L
printf 'a' > L3
file -f L
file -f L a
file a -f L
file -f L -b a
file -bf L
file -fL3
file --files-from L
file --files-from=L3
printf 'a\n' | file -f -
file -f L -f L3

cases.purpose: G71: listed names that are empty or missing are reported on stdout (status 0, 1 with -E); an unopenable NAMEFILE fails with status 1 before the operands.
cases.script:
printf 'x\n' > a
printf 'a\n\nnope\n' > L2
file -f L2
rc=0; file -E -f L2 || rc=$?; echo E-rc=$rc
rc=0; file -f missing a || rc=$?; echo missing-rc=$rc

cases.purpose: G71: -s / --special-files reads character devices as ordinary files (empty, data) instead of naming the device type; regular files are unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'x\n' > a
file /dev/null
file -s /dev/null
file --special-files /dev/null a
file -s -b /dev/zero
file -sL /dev/null
